nodes.label: Lazy Secret Loading Pattern
nodes.rationale: database_config/finnhub_config resolve AWS Secrets Manager values via module-level __getattr__ only on attribute access; importing the resolved value directly (from x import Y) freezes the secret into the importing module's namespace permanently at import time, with no way to swap credentials later, including during pytest collection. A real incident (a downstream consumer's 'flaky' test silently hit the real InfluxDB instead of a local Docker container) motivates always accessing via module.ATTR.

nodes.label: forex.util Self-Contained Utilities
nodes.rationale: forex/util/ is a self-contained in-house copy of the InfluxDB client, AWS secret loader, and time-unit constants, not a vendored copy of an external package, so the project has zero dependency on an external private repo. New shared utility code should be added to forex/util/ rather than reintroducing an outside import.

nodes.label: CHANGELOG Update Convention
nodes.rationale: CHANGELOG.md must be updated whenever code changes, with an entry under [Unreleased] using Keep a Changelog categories; version headers correspond to pyproject.toml's version field so a new version number must not be invented without also bumping pyproject.toml.

nodes.label: Dormant Pipelines Policy
nodes.rationale: economic_calendar_flow and positioning_flow are intentionally not live: Finnhub's free tier 403s on the calendar endpoint, and Oanda discontinued the order-book/position-book endpoints for retail accounts. Both are fully implemented and tested; they are dormant on cost/access grounds, not broken, and should not be 'fixed' by silently swallowing the error.

nodes.label: DST-Aware Grid Logic Gotcha
nodes.rationale: H4/D candles anchor to local wall-clock time, not a fixed UTC offset, so the DST-aware expected-bar grid logic in ForwardFillInator is fixed but subtle; read the README's 'DST-aware expected-bar grid' comment block before changing compute_df_all_time_diff_market_open or the grid construction.

nodes.label: is_forward_filled Tag Semantics
nodes.rationale: is_forward_filled distinguishes real bars from imputed ones; a forward-filled bar has zero return/volatility by construction, so this tag must never be stripped or treated as equivalent to real data downstream.

nodes.label: src-layout Package Convention
nodes.rationale: This is a src-layout, PyPI-publishable package (pip install -e '.[dev]', python -m build); every internal import uses the installed package name (from forex.etl.models import CandlestickRecord), never a relative path or sys.path hack.

nodes.label: DST-Aware Expected-Bar Grid Fix
nodes.rationale: The old grid used a fixed number of UTC seconds between bars forever (np.arange), fine for H1/M15 (fixed UTC-anchored) but wrong for H4/D (anchored to local 5pm America/New_York-style rollover), which silently drifted out of alignment twice a year at DST transitions. Confirmed against real EUR/USD history: H1/M15 had zero misaligned rows; H4/D had ~66% misaligned, with the first bad row landing exactly on the 2010-03-14 US Daylight Time switch. Fixed by building the grid in local wall-clock time and localizing per-instant (verified zero misaligned rows across 17 years of H4 history). Already-ingested forward-filled H4/D history needs one full re-run of forward_fill_flow to pick up the correction, since pull_data() always re-pulls the full history from cutoff_timestamp.

nodes.label: Swap-Rate Pipeline
nodes.rationale: A single current snapshot of long/short financing (rollover) rates per instrument, not a historical time series like candlesticks, so it has no ETL/pipeline/QA class hierarchy -- just SwapRateETL directly.

nodes.label: Economic-Calendar-Event Pipeline (blocked)
nodes.rationale: Not sourced from Oanda; comes from Finnhub with its own API key. /calendar/economic returns 403 on Finnhub's free tier (confirmed with a valid key); the paid tier is priced outside this project's budget. Code is complete and unit-tested, abandoned for now on cost, not because it's broken.

nodes.label: Positioning-Bucket Pipeline (blocked)
nodes.rationale: One row per price bucket per snapshot rather than a collapsed overall %-long/short stat, so a downstream consumer computes whatever aggregate it needs from the raw buckets; a snapshot can carry 100+ buckets per instrument per book type. Confirmed against both practice and live accounts that OANDA discontinued orderBook/positionBook entirely as a business decision, now offered only via a $1,850/month enterprise product with a $22,000/year minimum -- abandoned on cost, not a bug.

nodes.label: Market-Hours Gate
nodes.rationale: check_market_open_task no-ops any run outside forex trading hours (Fri 17:00 ET -> Sun 17:00 ET), so no extra cron filtering is needed on scheduled deployments.

nodes.label: Scheduled Deployment Table (serve.py)
nodes.rationale: serve.py registers nine deployments across candlestick, forward-fill, and swap-rate flows -- one candlestick-fetch deployment per granularity, each paired with a forward-fill deployment offset 10 minutes later so it runs against freshly-landed candles rather than racing the fetch feeding it.

nodes.label: 14 Tracked Instruments Rationale
nodes.rationale: Seven FX majors plus XAU/USD (gold, added 2026-07-14 to test whether a different asset class carries more signal than heavily-arbitraged FX majors) and six FX crosses added the same window for the same reason.

nodes.label: H4 Hourly Polling Rationale
nodes.rationale: candlestick-H4/forward-fill-H4 poll every hour rather than every 4 hours at a guessed boundary offset because OANDA's exact H4 candle-close alignment (UTC vs NY-anchored, DST behavior) isn't confirmed; since CandlestickETL resumes from the last stored timestamp, over-polling just finds nothing new rather than risking silently missing candles for hours.

nodes.label: swap-rate-D 20:45 UTC Timing Rationale
nodes.rationale: Runs about 15 minutes before the 5pm New York rollover cutoff (a fixed UTC time, not DST-aware, the same simplification forex-ML's own trading-session features already make) so a fresh rate is on hand right as any held position would actually be charged one.

nodes.label: forward_fill_it/dropna Ordering Bug
nodes.rationale: account_for_holiday_market_closure() used to run before forward_fill_it() and call a bare dropna() (no subset=), dropping every row with any missing OHLCV value -- i.e. every gap, not just holiday closures -- which made forward_fill_it()'s ffill() a no-op. Fixed by reordering so forward_fill_it() runs first, and narrowing the closure-drop to rows still NaN after forward-filling. A TODO remains to replace it with an explicit holiday calendar so extended closures (e.g. Christmas week) get dropped/flagged instead of bridged over with a stale price.

nodes.label: Package Reorg to src/forex/ Layout
nodes.rationale: Reorganized into a PyPI-publication-friendly src/forex/ layout (previously etl/, flows/, oanda/, eda/, critical_timezone.py at repo root), with __init__.py added to every package directory, and pyproject.toml declaring a full hatchling build so the package installs and builds as a real wheel.

nodes.label: ci/vendor/ Workaround Removed
nodes.rationale: CI no longer needs the 'checkout to a forex/ directory' workaround now that the package is genuinely importable once installed; the old CI-only ci/vendor/ workaround is removed since forex.util now carries the needed modules directly.

nodes.label: requirements.txt/requirements-dev.txt Removed
nodes.rationale: Superseded by pyproject.toml's dependencies / optional-dependencies.dev.

nodes.label: forex-ML (downstream project)
nodes.rationale: Downstream consumer that uses is_forward_filled to distinguish real market data from imputed bars, and whose forex_ml/data/swap_rates.py reads the swap-rate measurement to account for rollover cost in triple-barrier labeling.

nodes.label: python_tools_and_shortcuts (private repo)
nodes.rationale: Private repo this project formerly depended on for get_secret, InfluxDbTool, and time_conversions; those three modules were ported into src/forex/util/ so the package no longer depends on it at all, in CI or otherwise.
